clue.text: Bound over for three months

definitions.meaning: to bound is to leap, a synonym for jump up
the season from March to May in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: A court binds someone over to keep the peace for a quarter of a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound over' is a British legal phrase for a court order, but here 'Bound' stands alone as a leap and 'over for' only links it to the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap is a jump, and the season after winter lasts about a quarter of the year.

clue.text: But he's an odd sort to get tanned

indicators.note: an odd sort of thing is a strange version, so these letters come out rearranged

parts.note: the letters B, U, T, H, E, S, A, N are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a peculiar fellow likes to bake brown in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd sort' wants to describe a person, but 'an odd sort' signals a rearrangement of BUT HE'S AN; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying out in the sun is how people darken their skin.

clue.text: Purpose of treatment for soldiers laid up

parts.note: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word laid is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Army men are bedridden, so they need medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is a British Army corps. In a down clue 'up' reads a word from bottom to top. The definition is loose: the answer describes what treatment aims at.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrective work is intended to put something right, the aim of any cure.

clue.text: One is distracted by northern light

indicators.note: someone distracted is all over the place, so the word one is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone's attention is caught by the aurora borealis in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is distracted' rearranges ONE to EON, and 'by' sets it beside N.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas glows red in advertising tubes, giving off illumination.

clue.text: You can't miss this store entrance

parts.note: a barn is a farm building for storing grain or hay
a door is the way in to a building

explanation.surface: A warning sign insists that the warehouse doorway is impossible to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: Something as broad as the side of a barn is the proverbial target nobody could fail to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'couldn't hit a barn door' mocks a hopeless shot, so a huge target is what nobody misses.

clue.text: Surprise shots at men in melee

indicators.note: a melee is a confused brawl, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: twelve letters of anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Bystanders are startled when gunfire is aimed at soldiers in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in melee' looks like part of a battle scene; it signals that SHOTS AT MEN IN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is the feeling of being taken unawares.

clue.text: Steer straight

definitions.meaning: a bullock; an old word for cattle
undiluted, as a drink served without water or mixer

explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for oxen, and a spirit served without water, also called undiluted.

clue.text: Decorated about noon, has to deliver a speech

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally in public

explanation.surface: An honoured person must give a talk around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link; 'about' puts ORATE around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is heavily ornamented or embellished.

clue.text: What I'd be doing in the circus?

definitions.text: What I'd be doing in the circus?

indicators.note: in places the word I'd within the arena word

parts.note: a circus performs in a ring
the contraction gives its letters I and D

explanation.surface: A clown wonders what act they would perform under the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: a circus rider performs in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseback acts are a staple of the circus ring.

clue.text: Part of an Elgar composition — in D Minor?

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters D, M, I, N, O, R are arranged anew

parts.note: the musical key gives the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A music lover asks whether a movement of an Elgar piece is written in D minor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' reads as Elgar's work but signals the rearrangement of D MINOR; the definition is 'Part of an Elgar' (work). The famous movement is ninth of the Enigma Variations.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth of Elgar's Enigma Variations bears this name, after the biblical hunter.

clue.text: Coach in Latin but becoming overworked

indicators.note: in places the coaching word inside the Latin word

parts.note: sed is the Latin word for but
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A tutor teaches Latin, but finds the work exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link. 'Latin but' means the Latin for 'but', SED, which holds TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pushed too hard is under strain, tense from excessive effort.

clue.text: A good turn-out of servicemen and women?

definitions.text: A good turn-out of servicemen and women?

parts.words: A good turn-out of servicemen and women?
parts.note: a turn-out is a military muster, and a good one here is a godly one: troops marching to Sunday worship

explanation.definitionFit: A formal muster of troops who march to attend a religious service.

clue.text: General assistant

parts.note: reads as a general dogsbody, but means the officer who helps an army general

explanation.definitionFit: An aide-de-camp is the officer who assists a senior commander, and the short form means any helper.

clue.text: It's often used for tea round at home

definitions.text: It's often used for tea round at home

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for tea encloses the other piece

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
in means at home

explanation.surface: A hostess brings out the good tableware when serving tea to guests in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition of porcelain tableware, and it is also the wordplay, with 'round' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain is the traditional material for teacups and teapots.

clue.text: School where one changes form about the beginning of term

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the rearranged word encloses a letter
to change form is to take a new shape, so the letters of one are rearranged
the first letter of the word term

explanation.surface: At a boarding school, a pupil moves to a new class as term starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes form' suggests moving up a school year, but it rearranges ONE into EON, which goes 'about' the T from 'the beginning of term'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English public school near Windsor, founded in 1440.

clue.text: It's bound to include maps

parts.note: reads as 'certain to contain charts', but bound means bound as a book

explanation.surface: Something is certain to feature charts.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps, bound between covers.

clue.text: Boring bit of exercise

definitions.meaning: the tool tip that bores holes
a training routine, as in a fire or army practice

explanation.definitionFit: A tool for making holes, and also a practice routine such as parade-ground training.

clue.text: Where they are well, equipped to deal with complaints?

definitions.text: Where they are well, equipped to deal with complaints?

parts.words: Where they are well, equipped to deal with complaints?
parts.note: read without the comma it praises an efficient service desk; with it, a place of wells and spas for treating ailments

explanation.definitionFit: A spa town where visitors go to recover from illness.

clue.text: Gamble on mine product sample

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a gamble

indicators.note: a product is what is made from something, so the letters of mine are reworked

explanation.surface: A speculator bets on output from a mine before testing an ore sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' reads as output from the mine but signals rearranging MINE to IMEN, placed under SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: An example taken for testing or display is an instance of its kind.

clue.text: Southern voter who prefers one to another

parts.note: an elector is a person entitled to vote

explanation.surface: A voter from the south favours one candidate over a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase acting as a noun: someone who chooses, such as a picker of a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chooses is making a choice between candidates.

clue.text: To take a course like this is humiliating

definitions.text: To take a course like this is humiliating

parts.words: To take a course like this is humiliating
parts.note: a course here is a dish at a meal, a pie of offal, the humble fare of servants

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to admit you were wrong and accept the humiliation.

clue.text: Father Thomas will evoke pity

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Thos is a traditional abbreviation of the name Thomas

explanation.surface: A priest named Thomas will stir compassion in his flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will evoke' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality that arouses sorrow or sympathy.

clue.text: Standard stopper

explanation.definitionFit: A flag carried aloft, and also one who prohibits something.

clue.text: Woe is me, giving back part of my salary

indicators.note: giving back means returning, so the extracted letters are read backwards
part of means some letters are taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: An employee laments having to return a slice of their wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' picks SALA from within 'salary', and 'giving back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret, like a cry of sorrow.

clue.text: Jack points to high lakes

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor; tar alone also means sailor
N, north, is a point of the compass
S, south, is another compass point

explanation.surface: A sailor points the way towards some mountain lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a crossword word for a sailor, TAR. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mountain lakes in northern England's hills.

clue.text: One covering end of chin in spots

indicators.note: covering means going over and around, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: the last letter of the word chin

explanation.surface: A single plaster hides the tip of someone's chin in a breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'covering' puts ACE around N, the 'end of chin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin condition producing pimples, typical in teenagers.

clue.text: Floppy disc-I'm into that

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: LP, a long-playing record, is a disc
the contraction gives its letters I and M

explanation.surface: A computer user says they are keen on floppy discs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floppy disc' reads as old computer storage, but 'Floppy' is the definition. An LP is a long-playing record; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking firmness, drooping and slack.

clue.text: There's an atmosphere when Laura goes topless

indicators.note: topless means losing the top letter, the first of Laura

explanation.surface: Things get charged when a woman named Laura strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There's' and 'when' are links. In a down clue the top of a word is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive feeling or air surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: The best runners suffer a set-back at the start of this race

definitions.text: The best runners suffer a set-back at the start of this race

parts.words: The best runners suffer a set-back at the start of this race
parts.note: in this kind of race the strongest runners are given a disadvantage, starting behind or carrying extra weight

explanation.definitionFit: A race where better competitors are burdened so that all have an equal chance.

clue.text: Top medal received in action

indicators.note: something received in another thing is taken inside it

parts.note: a suit is a legal action
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: A soldier is decorated for bravery in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' suggests battle, but it is a lawsuit. The Military Medal is a British gallantry award.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or highest point of a mountain.

clue.text: Took off for hurried round trip

indicators.note: round means placed around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: sped means went fast
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone set off quickly for a journey there and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round trip' reads as one phrase, but 'round' is the container signal and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Removed clothing, as one undresses.

clue.text: Ring master?

parts.note: not a circus ringmaster but the composer of the Ring cycle of operas

explanation.definitionFit: The German composer of the four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen.
